title: Qualified Intermediary Coordination
name: Qualified Intermediary Coordination
metaTitle: Qualified Intermediary Coordination in Jacksonville, FL
metaDescription: Sequencing a Jacksonville qualified intermediary engagement across JAXPORT industrial, Southbank medical, and Duval County closings before funds ever move.

sections.html: A signed exchange agreement means nothing to a Jacksonville closing table if it arrives after the relinquished sale has already funded. That single sequencing failure disqualifies more exchanges than any dispute over an identified property ever does, and it is the first item checked before anyone touches notices, assignments, or a closing calendar. Everything else in a Jacksonville exchange is downstream of whether the qualified intermediary was under contract before the wire ever left the closing agent's trust account.

sections.heading: Locking In the QI Before the Sale Contract Is a Week Old
sections.html:
Choosing a qualified intermediary works best treated like a sole-source award: the decision needs to be final before funds obligate, not negotiated after the fact. A Jacksonville seller who waits until closing week to shop QI providers has already narrowed the field to whoever can turn around an exchange agreement overnight, which is rarely the provider best suited to a JAXPORT-adjacent industrial sale or a Southbank medical office disposition. Locking in that selection the same week the sale contract is signed keeps the exchange agreement, the assignment language, and the closing instructions moving on one calendar instead of three.

Every day that selection slips past the sale contract's execution date is a day the relinquished closing can outrun the paperwork, and once that closing funds, there is no remedy that reopens the exchange after the fact.

sections.heading: The Constructive-Receipt Line the File Has to Show Was Never Crossed
sections.html:
Constructive receipt is the one failure a qualified intermediary cannot paper over later: if sale proceeds land in the investor's own account for even an afternoon, the exchange ends regardless of what documents get produced afterward. A file built to hold up under later review shows, item by item, that the money never had a path back to the seller.

  • Wire instructions on both closings naming the qualified intermediary's account, not the investor's
  • Assignment of the relinquished sale contract executed before that closing funds
  • Assignment of the replacement purchase contract executed before that closing funds
  • Written identification delivered to the QI inside the 45-day window
  • Settlement statement on each closing showing funds routed directly to or from the QI
  • Lender notified of the exchange structure before underwriting on the replacement loan begins

sections.heading: Southbank Medical and JAXPORT Industrial Don't Close on the Same Calendar
sections.html: A Southbank medical office disposition and a JAXPORT-adjacent distribution building rarely move through diligence at the same pace. Medical space carries tenant estoppel and licensure paperwork that can push a closing date later than planned, while an industrial building near the port corridor more often waits on a lender's appraisal to catch up to what comparable properties along I-95 and I-10 have actually traded for. Coordinating notices across both a straightforward one-for-one exchange and a multi-asset disposition means tracking two separate closing calendars against the same 45-day identification clock, not assuming both sides land on the date first discussed with the broker.

sections.heading: What Duval's Consolidated Assessment Changes on the Settlement Statement
sections.html: Duval County runs consolidated city-county government, which means one assessor's office handles valuation for both a downtown high-rise and a Westside industrial parcel, and that consolidation shows up on a closing settlement statement as a single tax proration line rather than the separate city and county entries an out-of-state investor might expect from a prior transaction elsewhere. Confirming how the closing agent is prorating that assessment before the closing date, rather than during it, keeps a funds-flow question from surfacing the same week the qualified intermediary is trying to release proceeds for a replacement purchase.

sections.heading: Closing the File the Way an Examiner Would Expect to Find It
sections.html: Once the replacement property closes, the qualified intermediary's file is the record an examiner would pull first if the exchange is ever questioned years later. A complete file holds the exchange agreement, both assignment documents, the written identification notice, settlement statements from both closings, and lender correspondence acknowledging the exchange structure. Requesting that full package directly from the QI, rather than assuming it arrives unprompted, and routing a copy to the investor's tax advisor closes the file the same way whether the underlying asset was a Southbank office suite or a distribution building off I-95.

faqs.q: What is the one deadline that matters most for a Jacksonville qualified intermediary engagement?
faqs.a: The exchange agreement has to be signed and the QI under contract before the relinquished property's closing funds, since the structure cannot be created retroactively once proceeds have reached the investor. Locking in that selection the same week the sale contract is executed is the step that protects everything downstream.

faqs.q: How does Duval County's consolidated government affect the closing settlement statement?
faqs.a: Because Duval runs a single consolidated assessor's office rather than separate city and county entries, tax proration on the settlement statement appears as one combined line, which can look unfamiliar to an out-of-state investor used to two separate entries. Confirming that proration with the closing agent before the closing date avoids a last-minute funds-flow question.

faqs.q: Does a Southbank medical office exchange move on the same timeline as a JAXPORT industrial exchange?
faqs.a: Not usually. Medical space carries estoppel and licensure documentation that can extend diligence, while industrial buildings near the port corridor more often wait on a lender appraisal to catch up to recent comparable sales. Both still answer to the same 45-day identification clock even when the closing calendars differ.

faqs.q: What triggers constructive receipt on a Jacksonville exchange, and how is it avoided?
faqs.a: Constructive receipt happens the moment sale proceeds could reach the investor's own account, even briefly, and it disqualifies the exchange regardless of intent. Wire instructions naming the qualified intermediary directly on both closings, confirmed against the settlement statement before the closing date, keep that line from being crossed.

faqs.q: What should be in the qualified intermediary's file once a Jacksonville replacement property closes?
faqs.a: A complete file includes the exchange agreement, both assignment documents, the written identification notice, settlement statements from both closings, and any lender correspondence acknowledging the exchange. Requesting that package directly from the QI and forwarding a copy to the investor's tax advisor is what closes the file properly.
